Ben —

Thanks. I've started the SSQ draft and focused on the PII-handling sections. Key points in the draft (attached):

- Data classification: we use a 4-tier schema (Public / Internal / Confidential / PII). The attached CSV maps common API fields to PII categories and default retention buckets (30d/90d/1yr/indefinite).
- Pseudonymization/tokenization: for Hosted mode we suggest tokenization of user identifiers at the ingestion layer. Customers can enable per-tenant tokenization in Dedicated/Private via our tokenization plugin.
- Access controls: principle of least privilege + role-based access (RBAC). Attached doc includes the role-to-permission matrix and sample queries used to generate an IAM export.
- Subprocessors: current list included in the SSQ draft. Note — some subprocessors vary by region; we'll flag regional subprocessors in the final package.
- Retention and deletion: API-level record deletion triggers async purge from cache and downstream exports; long-term backups are retained per customer SLA; we note exceptions for legal holds.

Attachments: redwood_ssq_answers_draft_v1.docx, data_classification_matrix.csv

Jonas — can you add the updated data-flow PNG and the KMS attestation blurb? If you can provide an IAM export sample (obfuscated) and a sample audit log line, we can include both in the final ZIP.

I can turn this into a concise cover letter for Aetna once we have Jonas's pieces.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole | Privacy Lead

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Ben / Marissa —

Adding infra artifacts. Highlights:

- Data flow diagram (attached) shows three runtime paths. Hosted traffic is routed through our multi-tenant ingress, tokenized at the edge for configured fields, then routed to ephemeral worker pools. Dedicated routes bypass multi-tenant shared cache and can be pinned to region-specific clusters. Private (VPC/on-prem) stays within customer network; we annotate any cross-region egress with explicit controls.
- Encryption: all data is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest. For hosted keys we manage KMS with HSM-backed keys; for Dedicated/Private customers we support customer-managed keys (CMKs) and provide an attestation export (attached PDF) showing key rotation policy and current key ARNs.
- Access evidence: attached is an obfuscated IAM export and a one-line audit log sample demonstrating a least-privilege access event (service account assuming inference-worker role restricted to dataset-id). We can produce a curated set of audit log extracts under NDA if they need raw logs.
- Subprocessors: infra-related subprocessors (monitoring, storage) are included; see SSQ draft for full list.

Attachments: redwood_dataflow_routing_v2.png, kms_attestation_export.pdf, iam_export_sample.json (obfuscated)

If we want to send a consolidated package to Aetna today I'll bundle Marissa's draft + my attachments + a short cover note. Otherwise I can queue additional audit slices tomorrow.

--Jonas
